statement: The formal slice construction. Let $\mathcal M$ be a $\mathbb U$-small category with pullbacks, let $W$ contain the isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and let $\mathcal L$ contain the isomorphisms and be stable under composition and pullback. The same assertion holds for a larger category when all the localizations below exist in the chosen larger universe. For $S\in\mathcal M$, put \[ W_S^{\mathcal L}=\{u:X\to Y\text{ in }\mathcal M/S: u\times_S T\in W\text{ for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L\}. \] This class contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three, and is contained in $W_S$, the class detected on total objects. If $W$ is closed under retracts, so is $W_S^{\mathcal L}$. Every postcomposition functor $\Sigma_f:\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M/T$, for $f:S\to T$, preserves these classes. If $f\in\mathcal L$, strict pullback $f^{-1}:\mathcal M/T\to\mathcal M/S$ also preserves them and the ordinary adjunction $\Sigma_f\dashv f^{-1}$ descends to both the ordinary and enhanced localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.1 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Raw slice adjunction only along the testing class; all postcomposition functors descend.

statement: Arbitrary raw pullback does not follow. The hypotheses of E.1 do not imply that raw pullback preserves the fine classes for every $f$. In the presheaf fine theory of $\Cat/[1]$, the inclusion $u:e_1\to[1]$ over $[1]$ is a fine equivalence, whereas its pullback along $e_0\to[1]$ is $\varnothing\to e$, which is not. Consequently the inverse image on the fine localization, when it exists, cannot in general be computed by raw pullback.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.2 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Exact endpoint counterexample; ef_finite_checks.py.

statement: A recognition theorem giving all three Kan functors. Suppose that the enhanced localizations $\mathscr E(S)=(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^{\mathcal L})^{-1}]_\infty$ exist for bases $S$ in a category $\mathcal B$. Suppose we are given a functor $C:\mathcal B\to\Cat_\infty$ with small values and fully faithful functors $h_S:C(S)\to\mathscr E(S)$ satisfying the following precise presentation hypotheses. The category $\mathscr E(S)$ has all small colimits. Each functor $\Map(h_S(c),-):\mathscr E(S)\to\Spaces$ preserves all small colimits. These functors jointly detect equivalences. For each $f:S\to T$, postcomposition descends to a colimit-preserving functor $F_f:\mathscr E(S)\to\mathscr E(T)$ and there is a coherent equivalence $F_fh_S\simeq h_TC(f)$. Then the restricted Yoneda functors give equivalences \[ H_S:\mathscr E(S)\simeq\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces),\qquad H_S(X)(c)=\Map(h_S(c),X). \] Under these equivalences, $F_f$ is left Kan extension along $C(f)^{\op}$; it has right adjoint $f^*$, given by restriction, and this restriction has right adjoint $f_*$. These are coherent functors of the base, hence yield the requested pseudofunctors on homotopy categories. The locally constant subcategory has both adjoints to its inclusion. None of the presentation hypotheses is claimed to follow from E.1 or from factorization through intrinsic fibrations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.3 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Enhanced compact-projective presentation is an explicit extra hypothesis; it is not inferred from enough intrinsic fibrations.

statement: Coefficient localization and exact squares. In E.3 one may replace the coefficient category of spaces by any presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, once the slice presentation with those coefficients has been verified. In particular, an accessible reflective localization $L:\Spaces\to\mathcal V$ gives the objectwise localization \[ \Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces)\longrightarrow\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Restriction still has both Kan adjoints, and the locally constant subcategory is reflective and coreflective. For a strictly commuting square of ordinary indexing categories, base change for these Kan functors follows whenever its relevant comma-category comparison is homotopy final for left Kan extension, or homotopy initial for right Kan extension. In particular the presheaf left base-change map is invertible if the vertical map is $W_\infty$-smooth or the horizontal map is $W_\infty$-proper; the right map is invertible with these two roles reversed.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.4 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Presentable coefficient version; canonical mates and exact comma comparisons.

statement: Instances and the extra coarse comparison. For $W_\infty$, the presheaf fine localization of $\Cat/S$ satisfies E.3 with $C(S)=NS$ and $h_S(s)$ the point $e_s\to S$; the dual localization uses $NS^{\op}$. The contravariant and covariant simplicial model structures give the same instances over quasicategorical bases, with the proviso in Part B about raw strict slice tests over arbitrary simplicial sets. For finite Alexandrov posets with downsets open and unrestricted topological total spaces, the open-test localization is the covariant instance $C(P)=NP^{\op}$ proved in Part D. Discrete topological bases give the product of copies of spaces directly. The additional assertion that the coarse localization agrees with the locally constant part requires the coarse comparison \[ (\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\Spaces_{/BC(S)} \simeq\Fun(BC(S)^{\op},\Spaces) \] and compatibility of its localization functor with $\Lan_{q_S^{\op}}$. For $(\Cat,W_\infty)$ this comparison holds. It is not part of the abstract recognition hypotheses.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.5 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Coarse equals locally constant only after the extra coarse comparison.

statement: The coarse theory is not the locally constant fine theory for every localizer. Replacing $W_\infty$ by an arbitrary fundamental localizer in the coarse comparison of E.5 is false. Already for $W_0$, the component equivalences, and $S=BC_2$, the canonical coarse localization identifies two distinct locally constant objects of the fine theory.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.6 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: BC2 with component equivalences; fine local systems retain a regular action lost by total localization.

statement: What enough intrinsic fibrations supplies. Let $\mathcal M$ have a terminal object and pullbacks, and let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Define $\Fib_W$ by universal preservation of $W$ under strict pullback. Assume that every morphism factors as a map in $W$ followed by a map in $\Fib_W$. Then every map in $W\cap\Fib_W$ remains in $W$ after arbitrary pullback. Consequently the full subcategory of objects whose terminal map lies in $\Fib_W$, with these weak equivalences and fibrations, is a category of fibrant objects and presents the same enhanced localization as $\mathcal M$. It supplies finite homotopy limits and the usual homotopy-fibre construction. This does not identify the fine slice theories, and does not imply E.3.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.7 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.240–261; XIII ms.7–12; PATHS D.8,D.17,D.18
notes: Brown finite floor; no all-small strict diagram rectification.

statement: The accessible localizers satisfying the intrinsic factorization axiom. For an accessible fundamental localizer $W$ of $\Cat$, factorization through $\Fib_W$ is equivalent to aspherical generation of $W$, to generation by a set of maps $A\to e$, and to right properness of the associated Thomason model structure. In the corresponding accessible localization of spaces it is precisely nullification. Thus truncation localizers satisfy this factorization axiom; the nonzero-spectrum homology localizers in Part B do not. The right class of the associated modality is not the class $\Fib_W$: every $X\to e$ belongs to $\Fib_W$, whereas a terminal map is in that right class only when its fibre is local.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.8 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Necessity of aspherical generation does not use accessibility; model equivalences do.

statement: What a path object must supply. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has finite limits, $W$ has two-out-of-three, and $\mathcal A=\Liss\cap\Prop$ is stable under pullback and composition and contains product projections. Suppose functorially for each $S$ there is a path object \[ S\xrightarrow{c_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{(s_S,t_S)}S\times S, \qquad s_Sc_S=t_Sc_S=\id_S, \] whose endpoint map belongs to $\mathcal A$ and whose source evaluation $s_S$ is universally in $W$. Then every $f:X\to S$ factors functorially as \[ X\xrightarrow{i_f}X\times_{S,s_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{p_f}S \] with $i_f(x)=(x,c_Sf(x))$ in $W$ and $p_f=t_S\pr_2$ in $\mathcal A$. Merely requiring $c_S\in W$ and $(s_S,t_S)\in\mathcal A$ does not prove the required assertion about $i_f$; the transfer hypothesis must be supplied.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.9 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Universal source evaluation is required for the indicated mapping-path transfer.

statement: The groupoid test and the meaning of collapse. Let $S$ be a small groupoid and let $\mathcal M=\mathrm{Gpd}$ with categorical equivalences. For functors of groupoids over $S$, both comma-test classes agree with the total equivalences. Their enhanced localizations consequently agree with the coarse theory, which is the infinity-category of families of $1$-types over $NS$. Both variances are identified by inversion in $S$. This does not mean that every artificially chosen class $\mathcal L$ gives the coarse localization.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.10 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Proved ordinary-groupoid test; no dependence on the unrefereed globular model claim.

statement: The intermediate-subcategory assertion under replacement data. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks, let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and suppose that every arrow factors as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic $W$-fibration. Suppose in addition that for every base $S$ there is a functor \[ R_S:\mathcal M/S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_W S \] and a natural transformation $\eta_S:1_{\mathcal M/S}\to i_SR_S$ whose components are in $W_S$, where $i_S$ denotes the full inclusion. Then XII's axioms (a), (b), and (c), in their exact formulations A.10, hold. In particular, for every full subcategory $\operatorname{Fib}_W S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$, both inclusions induce equivalences at the restricted $W_S$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.11 and its proof (sections/E_b062.tex)
notes: Functorial coaugmented W-replacement proves the stronger intermediate assertion.

statement: A six-object counterexample to XIIc B062. The implication $\mathrm{(a)}+\mathrm{(b)}\Rightarrow\mathrm{(c)}$ of A.10 is false, even for a finite lattice and a strongly saturated class $W$. Both premises can hold at every base while the conclusion fails at one base. The same example refutes the assertion with infinity-categorical localizations in place of ordinary localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.12 and its proof (sections/E_b062.tex)
notes: Six-element lattice counterexample; both ordinary and enhanced localizations; a_b062_verify.py.

statement: Ordinary homotopy categories do not supply coherent gluing. A gluing theorem for the enhanced fine theories cannot in general be replaced by the same pullback or lax-pullback construction on their homotopy categories. The comparison $\Ho\Fun([1],\mathcal V)\to\Fun([1],\Ho\mathcal V)$ need not be faithful, even for $\mathcal V=D(\mathbb Z)$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.13 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Coherent arrow category differs from arrows in the homotopy category; derived integer-coefficient example.

statement: The precise modality and locally cartesian closed comparison. Let $L:\Spaces\to\mathcal V$ be an accessible reflective localization of spaces. The following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is a nullification; its local objects are closed under dependent sums over local bases, hence form a modality; the canonical map \[ L(X\times_Z A)\longrightarrow LX\times_Z A \] is an equivalence for every $X\to Z\leftarrow A$ with $A,Z$ local; and $\mathcal V$ is locally cartesian closed. Consequently these are additional equivalent conditions in E.8. The modality's left class consists of maps with $L$-contractible homotopy fibres and can be strictly smaller than the class inverted by $L$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part E, statement E.14 and its proof (sections/E.tex)
notes: Accessible localizations of spaces; explicit proof of the LCC converse using point diagrams.

statement: The operations supplied by Der 1--4. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all $\mathbb U$-small categories, with presheaf variance, satisfying Der 1--4: coproducts of indexing categories give products, evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, restriction has both Kan adjoints, and the pointwise comma formulas hold. Then every $f:X\to Y$ has \[ f_!\dashv f^*\dashv f_*:\D(X)\rightleftarrows\D(Y), \] where the display denotes the three functors with their usual alternating directions. For $A\in\D(X)$ and $y\in Y$ the formulas are \[ (f_!A)_y\cong\colim_{(y\backslash X)^{\op}} A, \qquad (f_*A)_y\cong\lim_{(X/y)^{\op}} A. \] The diagram under each limit is restriction along the forgetful functor to $X$, interpreted as a coherent diagram in the derivator. Comma squares are homotopy exact. Exact squares are closed under horizontal and vertical pasting, with the direction of their two-cell fixed. Strongness, pointedness and stability are not needed for these statements.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.1 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Der 1–4 and canonical mate pasting; no strongness assumed.

statement: The two strict base-change theorems and their converses. Consider a strict pullback square \[ \begin{tikzcd} X'\ar[r,"g'"]\ar[d,"f'"']&X\ar[d,"f"]\\ Y'\ar[r,"g"']&Y. \end{tikzcd} \] The canonical maps, with source category $\D(X)$ and target category $\D(Y')$, are \[ f'_!g'^*\longrightarrow g^*f_!,\qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^*. \] The first is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-smooth or $g$ is $W_\infty$-proper. The second is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-proper or $g$ is $W_\infty$-smooth. Conversely, $f$ is proper if its right comparison is invertible for every such square with space-valued presheaves and all coefficients; the dual assertion characterizes smoothness by universal left base change.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.2 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Converse tests terminal coefficients on the left adjoint mate, not on the original right comparison.

statement: Unrestricted pullback base change. The left or right Kan half is not a formalism satisfying its corresponding base-change identity for all strict pullback squares of $\Cat$. Failure already occurs for endpoint inclusions into $[1]$, with discrete finite coefficients. It also occurs with stable coefficients.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.3 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Empty endpoint pullbacks; exact finite checks and nonzero stable version.

statement: The projection formula on the smooth half. Let $\D$ be a symmetric monoidal derivator whose external tensor preserves homotopy colimits separately, in the sense of \citet[Definitions 3.23 and 3.25]{EFGPS2014b}. If $f:X\to Y$ is $W_\infty$-smooth, then for $A\in\D(X)$ and $B\in\D(Y)$ the canonical projection map \[ f_!(A\otimes f^*B)\longrightarrow f_!A\otimes B \] is invertible. More generally this map is invertible for an arbitrary $f$ when $B$ is locally constant. The external formula \[ (f\times\id_Z)_!(A\boxtimes C)\cong f_!A\boxtimes C \] holds for every $f$, every small $Z$, and every $C\in\D(Z)$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.4 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Internal formula for smooth maps or locally constant second coefficient; external formula for all maps.

statement: Monoidality alone does not give an internal projection formula for all maps. Even for space-valued or stable presheaves the projection formula of F.4 fails for a general functor. Thus the unqualified monoidality assertion in Lead 3 needs its map or coefficient hypothesis.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.5 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Monoidality alone is insufficient for the internal projection formula; finite endpoint check.

statement: The right projection formula and its precise restrictions. For any functor $f$ and any dualizable object $B$ of the monoidal category $\D(Y)$, the right projection comparison \[ f_*A\otimes B\longrightarrow f_*(A\otimes f^*B) \] is invertible. For proper $f$ it is also invertible whenever tensoring with $B_y$ preserves the homotopy limits indexed by $X_y^{\op}$, for every $y$. In a stable monoidal derivator this includes homotopy-finite fibres, for arbitrary $B$. Without such restrictions the right projection formula is false, even for a proper and smooth projection.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.6 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Global dualizability or pointwise preservation of fibre limits is stated explicitly.

statement: Exchange formulas obtained by taking mates. Suppose $\D$ is closed symmetric monoidal. For every $f:X\to Y$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,A) \cong\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,f_*A). \] For smooth $f$, put $f^!=f^*$ as the right adjoint of $f_!$. The projection formula then gives \begin{align*} f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(A,f^!B)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_Y(f_!A,B),\\ f^!\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,C)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,f^!C). \end{align*} The right adjoint mate of the left base-change isomorphism in F.2 is \[ f^*g_*\cong g'_*f'^*. \] All these isomorphisms have the coherence inherited from their specified adjunctions.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.7 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Closed exchange and right-adjoint mates; all source and target functors specified.

statement: Why the adjunction directions reverse. Define the opposite derivator by $\D^\vee(S)=\D(S^{\op})^{\op}$. Then \[ f_!^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_*^{\D})^{\op},\qquad f_*^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_!^{\D})^{\op}. \] Opposition of indexing categories exchanges incoming and outgoing lifting categories, hence exchanges smooth and proper maps. The reversal of the adjunction arrows additionally uses opposition of the coefficient categories. Base opposition alone supplies a comparison of the two fine theories over opposite bases; it is not a duality of coefficients over a fixed base. Nor need $\D^\vee$ be monoidal with a separately cocontinuous tensor.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.8 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Both coefficient opposition and base opposition are needed to reverse adjunctions.

statement: Open--closed extensions and stable recollement. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow X$ be a sieve and $i:B\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary cosieve. For a pointed derivator there are adjunctions \[ j^?\dashv j_!\dashv j^*\dashv j_* ,\qquad i_!\dashv i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^! . \] All four Kan extensions are fully faithful; $j_!$ and $i_*$ are extension by zero. In a stable derivator there are coherent fibre--cofibre sequences \[ j_!j^*A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_*i^*A, \qquad i_*i^!A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow j_*j^*A. \] Strongness is not needed for these coherent constructions. A triangulated recollement on the ordinary values follows when the stable derivator is strong.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.9 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Coherent sequences without Der5; strongness only for triangulated recollement.

statement: A correspondence formalism on the smooth class, with an enhancement. Let $\mathcal V$ be a $\mathbb V$-presentable closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category whose tensor preserves $\mathbb U$-small colimits separately. Regard the ordinary category $\Cat_{\mathbb U}$ as an infinity-category by its nerve, so its pullbacks are the strict categorical pullbacks. Put $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$. There is a lax symmetric monoidal functor \[ \Corr(N\Cat_{\mathbb U})_{E,\mathrm{all}} \longrightarrow\Cat_{\infty,\mathbb V},\qquad S\longmapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\mathcal V), \] sending a span $X\xleftarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}Y$, $b\in E$, to $b_!a^*$. It is a pre-six-functor formalism in \citet[Definitions A.5.1 and A.5.6]{EFMann2022} and a six-functor formalism in Definition A.5.7 there. The restriction to homotopy categories is the indicated half of the represented derivator. This assertion uses the given infinity-category, not merely its valuewise homotopy categories.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.10 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Base is nerve of ordinary Cat with strict pullbacks; enhancement and separate cocontinuity explicit.

statement: The terminology of the resulting operations. In F.10 every allowed map has $f^!=f^*$ and $f^!\one=\one$, compatibly with base change. Thus all these maps satisfy the cohomological smoothness formula with the trivial invertible twist; in the usual terminology for this identity they are cohomologically \emph{\'{e}tale}. This does not say that a Grothendieck-proper functor has $f_!=f_*$. Even a functor belonging to both Grothendieck classes need not have this ambidexterity. For a discrete bifibration with finite fibres, however, a stable coefficient category has the canonical ambidexterity $f_!\simeq f_*$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.11 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Kan exceptional inverse image is restriction; Grothendieck properness does not make left and right Kan functors equal.

statement: The all-smooth class does not satisfy the later diagonal convention. The class $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$ in F.10 is not closed under diagonals. Hence it is not a geometric setup under \citet[Definition 2.1.1 and Remark 2.1.2]{EFHeyerMann2024}, which add this requirement to the earlier convention. Restricting $E$ to discrete fibrations does satisfy the later convention and gives a six-functor formalism by the same construction. In that restriction the preceding cohomological \emph{\'{e}tale} description is unchanged.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.12 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: All-smooth class fails diagonal closure; discrete fibrations give a precise smaller setup.

statement: H\"ormann's diagram correspondences and the enhancement boundary. Fibered multiderivators encode the two halves and their exchange maps on the appropriate 2-multicategory of diagram correspondences. In \citet[Theorem 6.12]{EFHormann2017}, for pre-multiderivators $\mathbb E,\mathbb S$ satisfying Der 1--2, a strict morphism $\mathbb E\to\mathbb S$ is a left, respectively right, fibered multiderivator precisely when the induced map $\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb E)\to\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb S)$ is a 1-opfibration, respectively 1-fibration, of 2-multicategories. A closed monoidal derivator supplies the associated diagram-level six-operation structure. This does not turn all strict pullback squares of ordinary categories into exact squares and does not itself construct an infinity-categorical enhancement of an abstract derivator.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.13 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Theorem 6.12 is used with its actual pre-multiderivator hypotheses; no enhancement is manufactured.

statement: Comparison with relative smoothness and properness. For the indexed enhanced category $S\mapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ on the ordinary category $\Cat$ with strict pullbacks, the smooth and proper calibrations of \citet[Definition 2.3.1]{EFAnelWeinberger2025} are exactly $\Liss_{W_\infty}$ and $\Prop_{W_\infty}$ in our convention. This is a statement about that indexed category and that base category; replacing its base by $\Cat_\infty$ changes the pullback test.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.14 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Indexed presheaf calibration over the ordinary base Cat, not an unstated Cat-infinity pullback theorem.

statement: The genus-zero category and its geometric coefficients. For $n\geq3$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the pure orientation-preserving mapping class group of the $n$-punctured sphere. Let $\mathcal C_n$ have as objects the isotopy classes of essential multicurves, including the empty multicurve, and put \[ \Hom_{\mathcal C_n}(\sigma,\tau) =\{g\in\Gamma_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\Delta_\sigma, \qquad [h]\circ[g]=[hg], \] where $\Delta_\sigma$ is generated by the Dehn twists in the curves of $\sigma$ and acts on the right. Set $T_{0,n}=\mathcal C_n^{\op}$. The exit category of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$ with its dual-tree stratification is $N\mathcal C_n$. For every compactly generated presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, \[ \Shv_{\mathrm{cbl}}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C);\mathcal V) \simeq\Fun(N\mathcal C_n,\mathcal V) =\Fun(NT_{0,n}^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Forgetting the last mark induces $Q:\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$, $\sigma\mapsto q\sigma$, $[g]\mapsto[\phi(g)]$, and $F=Q^{\op}:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$. Here $q$ erases curves which become peripheral and identifies repeated isotopy classes, and $\phi:\Gamma_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma_n$ is the forgetful homomorphism.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.15 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Explicit mapping-class quotient category; stability range and coefficient hypotheses fixed.

statement: Forgetting a mark is proper and need not be smooth. For every $n\geq3$, $F:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$ is $W_\infty$-proper. For $n=4$ it is not $W_\infty$-smooth: a specified lifting category is equivalent to $B\mathbb Z$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.16 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Proper for every n>=3; at n=4 an incoming lifting category is BZ, so not smooth.

statement: Geometric direct image and the boundary squares in this example. In the coefficient equivalence of F.15, the categorical right Kan functor $F_*$ is the ordinary topological direct image of constructible sheaves for $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n+1}(\mathbb C)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$. Categorical right base change agrees with topological proper base change for point fibres and for the squares obtained by a closed boundary inclusion. A boundary is represented by the replete full cosieve in the entrance category whose multicurves contain a curve with the specified label partition. The left Kan half supplies no universal smooth base-change statement for this forgetful functor.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.17 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA geometric direct image and boundary base change
notes: Constructibility checked; fibre exit categories and replete boundary cosieves identify the canonical comparisons.

statement: Indexing an abstract derivator by strict higher categories. For a specified extension of an ordinary derivator to strict $n$-categorical indexing shapes, $2\leq n\leq\omega$, with lax or colax comma objects and a chosen Street-nerve weak-equivalence class, does the corresponding universal smooth/proper lifting condition imply the two base-change isomorphisms of F.2, with coherent mates? We have not established this statement. Even $n=2$ requires an explicit higher Der~4 and an invariance theorem for the chosen lax comma construction; neither is part of an ordinary derivator on $\Cat$. The model-structure claim discussed in Part C supplies neither datum. No proof in Part F uses that unrefereed claim.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.18 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: No proof depends on OpenAI 2026; first undecided case n=2 needs a higher Der4 and mate compatibility.

statement: An exact proper class in the diagonally closed setup. In the discrete-fibration setup of F.12, take $\mathcal V=\Sp$ or $D(k)$ for a nonzero commutative ring $k$. For a discrete fibration $p:E\to S$, the following are equivalent: $p$ is cohomologically proper in \citet[Definition 4.6.1(b)]{EFHeyerMann2024}; after every strict base change its left and right presheaf Kan extensions are naturally equivalent; and $p$ is a discrete bifibration with finite fibres. Finiteness is pointwise and requires no uniform bound. For this class the canonical comparison $p_!\to p_*$ is the finite biproduct equivalence.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, Part F, statement F.19 and its proof (sections/F.tex)
notes: Exact cohomological properness classification for discrete fibrations with spectra or nonzero commutative-ring coefficients; canonical norm only after checking diagonal properness.
